title: Lease vs licence - a distinction that changes everything legally
p1: A document can say “agreement” on top and still create very different legal rights. The difference between a lease and a licence is not just a matter of wording — it can change who controls the property.
p2: Many people assume that paying rent automatically means they have a lease. That is not always true. A lease generally gives the tenant a legal interest in the property, often with a right to occupy it exclusively. A licence usually only gives permission to use the property without creating that same level of interest.
p3: The surprising part? Two people can use the same space, pay the same amount, and sign similar-looking papers, yet the law may treat them completely differently. The real test is often the nature of the arrangement, not the label on the document. Before signing, look beyond the title and understand the rights being created.
conclusion: Have you ever signed a rental or usage agreement without knowing whether it created a lease or only a licence?
